title: Are Deterministic Descriptions And Indeterministic Descriptions Observationally Equivalent?
locator: Search-result summaries of the arXiv and PhilSci listings; published Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics 40(3):232-242 (2009). Text not opened.
relevance: Nearest philosophical precedent: uses Ornstein theory to show that measure-theoretic deterministic systems and stochastic processes, Markov ones included, can be observationally equivalent. This note applies the same machinery to time reversal.
limits: Discovery only. Whether Werndl draws the time-reversal corollary is unchecked.

title: On isomorphism of weak Bernoulli transformations
locator: Advances in Mathematics 5 (1970) 365-394, as cited in search results; not opened.
relevance: Weak Bernoulli transformations with finite generator are isomorphic to Bernoulli shifts of equal entropy; two-sided mixing Markov shifts are weak Bernoulli (secondary reports). Input to the corollary that every mixing finite Markov chain is time-reversal symmetric as a measure-preserving system.
limits: Discovery only; the theorem's hypotheses are taken from secondary reports. The DOI is our inference from the citation and is not verified.
